name: @zoey/orb
description: Zoey Orb — the voice surface. Particle sphere, collapsed layout, one WebSocket in the main process.
$comment: NO "type": "module" — deliberate. CONTRACT §2.3 puts the WebSocket in main, and this app
runs with sandbox: true. A sandboxed Electron preload CANNOT be an ES module; it must be
CommonJS. Declaring the package as ESM makes electron-vite emit ESM for main AND preload,
and the preload then fails to load at runtime. Source is written as ESM TypeScript either
way; electron-vite transpiles main/preload to CJS and the renderer stays ESM via Vite.
@zoey/protocol and @zoey/tokens are devDependencies ON PURPOSE. electron-vite's
`build.externalizeDeps` (on by default for main and preload) externalises everything in
`dependencies`, and @zoey/protocol's entry is raw TypeScript (src/index.ts, which imports
./enums.generated.ts). Externalised, that becomes a runtime require() of a .ts file and main
crashes on launch. In devDependencies they are bundled, which is what we want.
The option is `build.externalizeDeps`, NOT the `externalizeDepsPlugin()` helper — that helper
is deprecated in electron-vite 5. It is still exported and still functional, so calling it
produces no warning and no failure; only the docs and the types say it is the old form.
`ws` stays a real dependency: it is externalised and required at runtime. Bundling it would
drag in its optional native deps (bufferutil, utf-8-validate) as unresolvable imports.
Versions are pinned exactly, never caret ranges — same rule the Console applies to xterm 6.
vite is 7.3.6, NOT the latest 8.2.1, and @vitejs/plugin-react is 5.2.0, NOT the latest 6.0.5.
This is a real peer-dependency ceiling, not caution: electron-vite@5.0.0 peers on
vite ^5 || ^6 || ^7, while plugin-react@6 peers on vite ^8 and drags in @rolldown/plugin-babel
and babel-plugin-react-compiler. plugin-react@5.2.0 peers on ^4 || ^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8 with no
extra peers, so 7.3.6 + 5.2.0 is the newest combination that resolves cleanly. Revisit when
electron-vite ships vite 8 support.
